messages:
maria (AM): Quick sync — new sealed-network POC with a regulated finance customer. They want signed sneakernet deliveries, offline activation, SBOM for every bundle, and a biweekly upgrade cadence. Can we operationally support this and what are the POC commercial levers?

 todd (Solutions): We can. Two packaging patterns: (A) full artifact bundle including runtime + model + manifest + sbom + signature, or (B) delta patches for infra/runtime only. Deltas save transfer size but require a small local patch agent.

 jane (Eng): Packaging notes from runtime:
 - We support OCI images (good for customers with registry inside their network) and tarball bundles for fully isolated sites. Typical sealed bundle: bundle-<date>.tar.gz, manifest.json, sbom.cdx.json, signature.sig.
 - Deltas are binary diffs of checkpoints + patch manifest; they need version-compatible KV cache schema or we must invalidate caches.
 - Quantized weight changes are messy as applying a delta may require re-quantization; for model weight changes we recommend full bundle.

 maria (AM): Customer mandates a fortnightly patch cadence for compliance. Does that align with our deliverables?

 jane (Eng): We can commit to fortnightly infra/security patches. Model rollouts should be on-request and scheduled (note in SOW). We'll document: "Fortnightly infra/security bundles; model updates scheduled per mutual agreement."

 kevin (Legal): Contract flags: exclude liability for model accuracy/regression investigations during the POC; include an embargoed vuln disclosure window (30 days) and emergency patching SLA. Also include export-control/ECCN check if customer region requires it.

 maria (AM): Offline activation options? USB/HSM/token?

 todd (Solutions): Two flows supported:
 1) One-time license JWT included in the bundle and validated locally (no network required). Customer runs activation CLI that verifies signature against our public key.
 2) HSM-backed attestations if customer pre-provisions an HSM or KMS blob — this increases onboarding time.

 Example activation (air-gapped host):
 ```bash
 # on isolated host
 redwoodctl activate --license ./license.jwt --bundle ./redwood-bundle-2026-03-15.tar.gz --pubkey /etc/redwood/pubkey.pem
 ```
 This performs signature verification locally; no callback to the control plane.

 jane (Eng): Important: if they want telemetry disabled, set TELEMETRY_MODE=local in the config. Default control-plane telemetry is disabled for sealed bundles. Local traces go to /var/log/redwood/trace.log.

 maria (AM): Pricing asks: they want a 90-day POC and asked if Dedicated node pricing can be prorated. What's our position?

 todd (Solutions): POC commercial options we usually offer:
 - 30-day self-serve POC: standard trial with email support.
 - 90-day extended POC: charge 50% of monthly Dedicated list price pro-rated for duration, plus a one-time onboarding engineering fee to automate bundle generation and signing (estimate $5k–$12k depending on packaging complexity).
 - Reserved capacity for POC: requires a minimum throughput commit; discount if they sign an MOU.

 kevin (Legal): Add data-handling annex and indemnity cap for the POC SOW. Also require customer to confirm no export-restricted models will be imported.

 maria (AM): Security team also wants SBOM and CVE scan results for each bundle. Can we automate?

 jane (Eng): Yes — our CI emits CycloneDX SBOMs and we run distro/CVE scans. sbom.cdx.json is attached to every bundle and we include a short vulnerability summary in the manifest. Manifest includes sbom hash.

 todd (Solutions): Operational impact on upgrades: for infra-only bundles we recommend rolling updates across a two-node cluster to achieve <5 minutes perceived disruption. For single-node POCs a model swap will incur a brief outage (2–10 minutes depending on model size). Prefetching and prewarming KV cache reduces outage.

 jane (Eng): Prefetch/runbook example:
 ```bash
 # verify signature
 redwoodctl verify --bundle ./incoming.tar.gz --signature ./signature.sig --pubkey /etc/redwood/pubkey.pem
 # prefetch to warm caches
 redwoodctl prefetch --bundle ./incoming.tar.gz
 # schedule apply window
 redwoodctl apply --bundle ./incoming.tar.gz --rollback-point /var/backups/redwood-prev.tar.gz
 ```
 Rollback strategy: keep previous bundle snapshot and KV cache snapshot; apply is atomic after verification.

 maria (AM): Customer asked for a one-page runbook with commands and rollback steps for their security ops. Can we produce that?

 jane (Eng): I'll draft the one-pager with both full-bundle and delta workflows plus decision matrix (when to use each). Will include SBOM sample and a minimal CVE report template.

 tod d (Solutions): small typo, ack.

 todd (Solutions): I'll put together POC commercial options, exact pricing table, and recommend an onboarding fee range. I'll also propose an emergency patch SLA for the 90-day POC. :thumbsup:

 kevin (Legal): We'll prepare POC SOW clauses: telemetry opt-out, indemnity cap, export compliance, embargo window, and data-handling annex.

 ops-bot: Reminder: default hosted control-plane telemetry will be disabled for sealed deployments. Set TELEMETRY_MODE=local to avoid remote metrics. Scheduled follow-up set for 1778893600.

 maria (AM): Action items:
 - jane: deliver 1-page runbook + sample commands + sbom example by EOD Wed (1778976000)
 - todd: propose POC commercial options + onboarding fee estimate by EOD Tue (1778890000)
 - kevin: draft POC SOW clauses (telemetry opt-out, indemnity, export controls) by Thu

 jane (Eng): Ack. I'll include delta vs full-bundle guidance and a matrix of downtime/patch-size tradeoffs.

 todd (Solutions): Ack. I'll include pricing table and suggested SLAs for emergency patches.

 maria (AM): Thanks all, I'll share the runbook and commercial options with the customer tomorrow.

 ops-bot: Reminder set for 1778893600 to check progress on pricing.
